high.title: This Brazilian Stock Can Benefit Even from a 'Worst Possible Scenario' for Selic Rate, According to Analyst
high.summary: The Selic rate cutting cycle that began in March's COPOM meeting may be smaller than initially expected due to Middle East geopolitical tensions adding inflationary pressure. Market expectations for the terminal Selic rate have deteriorated from 12% to 13.5%-13.75% for end-2026, according to Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria. The analyst notes this revision occurred as geopolitical conflicts extend inflationary pressures beyond initial forecasts. Higher-than-expected rates typically pressure leveraged companies through increased debt service costs, creating headwinds for equity valuations. This shift in monetary policy expectations is critical for BRL traders and bond investors, as it suggests BCB may maintain a more hawkish stance longer than anticipated. Bond yields should remain elevated while BRL could face pressure from sustained high real rates. Investors should monitor geopolitical developments and upcoming COPOM communications for further guidance on the pace of rate cuts.

high.title: Vale (VALE3): Is It Time to Invest? Analyst Gives 5 Reasons to Buy Shares
high.summary: Vale shares fell 6% in March while Ibovespa dropped 0.9%, but Empiricus Research analyst Ruy Hungria calls the decline "unjustified." The stock recovered fully by April 15, closing at R$88.44 versus March's R$82.48 close. The analyst maintains a buy recommendation with five supporting reasons, suggesting the mining giant can continue "unlocking value" for investors despite broader market risk aversion that affected Brazilian equities in March.
